reasoning_traces.think:
The SRQC system defines a quotient abstraction α that maps concrete ledger events to abstract states, enabling local runtime checks without global model verification. The key insight is that α is designed to preserve safety properties under bounded refinement, allowing the system to detect violations of forbidden abstract states without re-running TLC or TLAPS proofs. This is achieved by collapsing concrete details (e.g., pending counts ≥2) into abstract classes (GE2), reducing complexity while maintaining safety guarantees. The local nature of admitUnderSRQC ensures that each invocation is validated against a fixed set of forbidden abstract states, making the system robust to runtime variability. The formal receipt job detects violations by observing when α maps a concrete state into a forbidden abstract state, triggering incident logging. This design supports both static verification and dynamic runtime monitoring, forming a dual-layered safety architecture.
